lessons.title: Introduction to Web Architecture & HTML
lessons.description: Understand how the web works, client-server models, HTTP requests, and the role of HTML in document structure.
lessons.notes: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser. Key concepts covered: DOCTYPE declaration, html, head, meta tags, and body hierarchy.

lessons.title: Semantic Tags, Media & Document Structure
lessons.description: Learn semantic elements such as header, nav, main, section, article, aside, and footer for optimal SEO and accessibility.
lessons.notes: Semantic elements clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer. Screen readers and search engine crawlers rely heavily on correct semantics.

lessons.title: HTML Forms, Validations & Input Types
lessons.description: Deep dive into form controls, inputs (text, email, password, date, radio, checkbox), labels, and HTML5 client-side validation attributes.
lessons.notes: Always associate form controls with descriptive `<label for='id'>` tags for screen reader accessibility and touch target hit area enlargement.

lessons.title: Quiz: HTML5 Basics & Semantic Markup
lessons.description: Test your grasp of HTML5 semantic tags, form elements, and accessibility best practices.

sections.title: Section 2: CSS3 Styling, Flexbox & Grid Layouts

lessons.title: CSS Cascade, Specificity & The Box Model
lessons.description: Understand how CSS rules resolve conflicts, the specificity hierarchy, margin collapsing, padding, borders, and content-box vs border-box.
lessons.notes: Always use `box-sizing: border-box;` in your global CSS reset to prevent unexpected layout breakage when modifying padding and borders.

lessons.title: Mastering CSS Flexbox Layouts
lessons.description: Master 1-dimensional layouts with Flexbox: flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, flex-wrap, flex-grow, and gap properties.
lessons.notes: Flexbox is ideal for navigation bars, responsive rows, vertical centering, and component-level UI distribution.

lessons.title: Assignment: Build a Responsive Landing Page
lessons.description: Create a fully responsive agency landing page with hero banner, feature cards, testimonial carousel, and a contact form.

lessons.title: JavaScript Variables, Functions & Scope
lessons.description: Learn modern ES6+ JavaScript syntax: let/const, arrow functions, template literals, closures, and scope chains.
lessons.notes: Use `const` by default and `let` only when reassignment is explicitly needed. Avoid `var` in modern JavaScript codebases.

lessons.title: Interactive DOM Events & Dynamic UI
lessons.description: Query DOM nodes, attach event listeners, handle form submit events, and render dynamic elements into the document tree.
lessons.notes: Event delegation on parent containers dramatically improves performance when dealing with large dynamic lists.

questions.question: Which HTML5 semantic element is best suited for self-contained content that could theoretically be distributed or syndicated independently (e.g., a blog post or news item)?
questions.explanation: The `<article>` element represents a complete, self-contained composition in a document, page, application, or site and that is, in principle, independently distributable or reusable.

questions.question: What is the primary accessibility purpose of associating an `<input>` with a `<label>` using the `for` and `id` attributes?

options.text: It automatically enables screen readers to announce the label and increases the clickable target area
It applies default CSS bold styling to the label text
It prevents the user from typing invalid email characters
It is required by browsers to submit data via POST

questions.explanation: Explicit association links the visual text directly to the input control for assistive technologies and enlarges the hit area for finger taps and mouse clicks.

questions.question: HTML is a Turing-complete programming language capable of executing dynamic computational algorithms.
questions.explanation: HTML is a declarative markup language that structures document content, not a general-purpose programming language with computational control flow.

questions.question: Which attribute on the `` tag is crucial for screen readers and search engines to understand image context?
questions.explanation: The `alt` attribute provides alternative descriptive text for users with visual impairments using screen readers and when the image fails to load.

forum.title: How do I horizontally and vertically center a div cleanly using modern CSS?
forum.content: I keep seeing multiple approaches (margins, transforms, flex, grid). What is considered the industry gold standard in 2026?

replies.content: The cleanest and most universally accepted approach today is either Flexbox: `display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;` or CSS Grid: `display: grid; place-items: center;`. CSS Grid's `place-items: center` is only two lines and works across all modern browsers!
Can confirm `place-items: center` with `min-height: 100vh` saved me hours on my landing page project!

forum.title: When should we prefer CSS Grid over Flexbox?
forum.content: Is it strictly 2D vs 1D layout, or are there real-world component scenarios where Grid is better even for 1D?
